items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: Morris Edwards worked with me out here in California before he even went to New York to live. He works with me.

ctx.x: music ever. It's the thing that's created right here in our own country, and it's unfortunate that it's not recognized as widely and as much as it is in other countries.

I got a letter just a few weeks ago from somebody wanting to get -- bring me -- from a Scandinavian booking agent. And I've gotten calls within the last year from people wanting me to go into Europe, you know. But my feeling now is that I would like to do something like that, if I have something going, some records going, you know, if the records were resurrected or reissued or something. But I think just to go someplace now just to be going, in the first place you've got to dicker and you've got to talk about…

So, if I'm fortunate enough to do that, but when you are doing a certain type of thing and you feel a certain type of rhythm, that I do, because I feel that what I'm doing, it's a sensitive -- I feel every movement that I make. I work really by my feeling, you know. When I play, that's the way I play the piano. I work strictly by feeling. And every musician -- any musician -- I don't say every -- but every musician who comes along doesn't feel this, you see. So there are certain people that I enjoy working with…
